review_notes:
I read the whole file and searched Mathlib for uses of its non-simp lemmas. I did not run Lean.

The simp set is small and consistent. `basis_repr_tmul` and `basis_apply` are `@[simp]` and rewrite to `a ⊗ₜ`/`1 ⊗ₜ` forms. `toMatrix_baseChange` is `@[simp]` and rewrites to `Matrix.map`, so it has no obvious loop or competing rule.

- **`basisAux_tmul`:** it is not simp, but `basis_repr_tmul` is the user-facing simp lemma. The proof of `basisAux_map_smul` uses `basisAux_tmul` explicitly.
- **`basis_repr_symm_apply`:** it is not simp. The general `Basis.repr_symm_single` lemma probably covers its left side, so I would not recommend a competing simp lemma. I did not confirm that.
- **`basis_repr_symm_apply'`:** with `basis_apply` as simp, `a • basis A b i` already normalizes through `1 ⊗ₜ b i`, so a simp attribute on it would be redundant.
- **`Basis.baseChange_linearMap` and `Basis.baseChange_end`:** these are not simp. The only external use I found is an explicit `rw [Basis.baseChange_end]` in `Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Polynomial.lean`. I found no evidence that making them simp would help, so I report nothing.

I found no justified simp-interface defect.
